metric_definitions.recall@k: gold chunks in the top k / gold chunks
metric_definitions.precision@k: gold chunks in the top k / k, even when fewer than k come back
metric_definitions.wrong_evidence: questions where a hard negative ranks above at least one gold chunk in the retrieved list (a gold chunk not retrieved ranks below all), or is cited anywhere in the raw answer / questions with hard negatives; by_relation counts a question under each hard-negative label that triggered, over the questions with a negative of that label; share_of_wrong is the share of wrong questions that label triggered (H3)
metric_definitions.exact_match: share of questions whose filter companies and periods both equal the labels
metric_definitions.companies_match: share of questions whose filter companies equal the tickers label
metric_definitions.periods_match: share of questions whose filter periods equal the fiscal_periods label
metric_definitions.filter_excluded_gold: gold chunks whose filing the filter excluded, summed over questions
metric_definitions.structural_citation_validity: cited chunk IDs that were among the retrieved chunks / cited chunk IDs, counted over every sentence of the raw answer, kept or dropped; null when nothing was cited
metric_definitions.dropped_share: sentences dropped by citation enforcement / sentences in the raw answers
metric_definitions.status: the answer's status line: answered, declined, not_found; no_status if the line was missing; refused if the API refused
metric_definitions.latency_ms: p50 and p95 per stage, by linear interpolation between the closest ranks; embed and retrieval (embed plus search) count only questions whose query embedding was made in this run; generation is each answer call's API latency when it was made, also for an answer replayed from the cache
metric_definitions.cost_usd: from the token counts each API reported and the header's dated price table; Voyage at list price, before any free allowance
metric_definitions.interval: percentile bootstrap 95% interval over 10000 resamples of the cell's questions, with replacement; each interval's generator is seeded by the header's seed and the interval's set, arm, class and metric; for a ratio, resamples with a zero denominator are left out and 'resamples' counts the rest
metric_definitions.directional: the cell has fewer than 10 questions in the scored split (research plan)
metric_definitions.judged: scored by an LLM judge, uncalibrated: no judge has been checked against hand scores yet; each metric runs 3 times as independent calls; a question's score is the mean of its runs that produced a value and its spread the highest run minus the lowest; a cell's mean is over its questions' scores, run_means is the cell mean within each run, spread is the highest run mean minus the lowest, and the interval resamples the questions' scores; a run with no value (skipped, undefined, or an unusable judge reply, which 'errors' counts) is left out
metric_definitions.faithfulness: Ragas faithfulness: statements in the kept sentences (citation markers removed) that the judge infers from the retrieved chunks / statements; skipped when no sentence was kept; no value when the judge finds no statements
metric_definitions.answer_relevancy: Ragas answer relevancy: mean cosine similarity (Voyage query embeddings) between the question and 3 questions the judge writes from the shown answer (citation markers removed), 0 if the judge calls every one noncommittal; skipped for an empty answer
metric_definitions.citation_support: kept sentences whose cited chunks, together, support every claim in them, per the judge / kept sentences; skipped when no sentence was kept
metric_definitions.judged_cost_usd: what judging cost (OpenAI judge calls plus Voyage embeddings for answer relevancy), over all runs; an evaluation cost, kept out of the operational cost_usd, which is what answering a question costs
metric_definitions.judge_usage: judge tokens over all runs as OpenAI reported them, replayed calls included: input_tokens includes cached_input_tokens and cache_write_tokens; output_tokens includes reasoning_tokens, which are shown separately and billed as output
metric_definitions.decline_correct: decline records: 1 if the judge finds the answer declined to advise
metric_definitions.not_found_correct: unanswerable records: 1 if the judge finds the answer said the filings lack the evidence without stating or guessing the fact
metric_definitions.graph: graph arms only: no_anchor counts questions that linked no anchor, empty_retrieval those whose retrieval held no chunk, not_found those answered not_found
metric_definitions.cypher_validity: graph_traversal only, per question: first_pass_valid when the first query passed the guard and ran without error in the timeout; valid_after_repair when the first or its one repair did; non_empty when one returned chunks; fallback when the question fell back to graph_local; null with no query
metric_definitions.graph_stages: anchor_linking, cypher_generation, cypher_repair and cypher_execution latency counts the questions that ran the stage; their cost is a mean over every question, a stage that did not run costing 0; search covers every stage after the query embedding

questions.question: Beyond lost direct sales, what knock-on competitive effects of U.S.-China export controls and trade tensions do NVIDIA, AMD and Intel describe in their latest 10-Ks?

answer.text:
NVIDIA says that being effectively foreclosed from China's data center compute market helped its competitors build larger developer and customer ecosystems to challenge it worldwide [0001045810-26-000021:0014]. It says licensing requirements have benefited certain competitors and encourage customers in China, the Middle East and other regions to pursue alternatives, including suppliers based in China, Europe and Israel [0001045810-26-000021:0043]. The Chinese government has encouraged customers to buy from China-based competitors and discouraged them from buying, importing or using NVIDIA's data center products [0001045810-26-000021:0015]. NVIDIA also says export controls may push customers outside China to "design-out" certain U.S. semiconductors, and may lead overseas governments to ask customers to buy from competitors instead [0001045810-26-000021:0045]. It adds that such controls may increase investment in foreign competitors that are less likely to be restricted by U.S. controls [0001045810-26-000021:0045]. It says the possibility of further controls has reduced demand and benefited competitors offering alternatives less likely to be restricted [0001045810-26-000021:0041]. NVIDIA says the controls have a disproportionate impact on it and may disadvantage it against competitors whose chips fall outside their scope [0001045810-26-000021:0044]. It also says China's government questioned whether H20 products have built-in vulnerabilities, which discouraged customers from purchasing them [0001045810-26-000021:0044]. Restrictions on data center GPUs may also reduce demand for its networking products used in servers containing those GPUs [0001045810-26-000021:0044].
These could make it harder to sell in, or restrict its access to, some markets [0000050863-26-000011:0072]. Intel says China has responded to U.S. restrictions with its own, including licensing requirements on critical minerals [0000050863-26-000011:0072]. It says the restrictions have in some instances reduced its sales and in a number of instances required specific governmental authorizations or exceptions [0000050863-26-000011:0072]. It says trade tensions have also affected customer ordering patterns and could result in reputational harm [0000050863-26-000011:0072]. Intel notes that Chinese semiconductor companies, including SMIC, are making significant investments, often with government support, in advanced technologies to develop products that compete with Intel's [0000050863-26-000011:0072].
For AMD, the excerpts describe only approximately $440 million of net inventory and related charges in 2025 tied to the U.S. government export control on AMD Instinct MI308 Data Center GPU products [0000002488-26-000018:0070].

questions.question: How do the climate and environmental-regulation risks described by NVIDIA, AMD and Intel in their latest 10-Ks differ, given that two are fabless and one runs its own fabs?

answer.text:
AMD lists environmental laws and conflict minerals regulations among its legal and regulatory risks, and separately lists climate change as a risk that may affect its business [0000002488-26-000018:0022]. It says its operations and those of its suppliers are subject to laws on materials used in products, manufacturing processes, pollutant discharge and waste handling [0000002488-26-000018:0049]. It says it cannot assure that they have been or will be in complete compliance, and violations could bring fines, suspended production, sales limitations or supply disruptions [0000002488-26-000018:0049].
It has been named a responsible party at three Superfund sites in Sunnyvale, California, and remains responsible for costs beyond its settlement agreements if the other parties don't fulfill their obligations [0000002488-26-000018:0049]. It also receives claims of alleged exposure to substances used in its former semiconductor wafer manufacturing facilities [0000002488-26-000018:0048].
On materials and climate, AMD says the EU and China restrict lead and other materials in electronic products, which could affect cost, quality and yields and lead to excess inventory [0000002488-26-000018:0050]. It says regulation of greenhouse gas emissions and climate-related risks could raise its energy costs, for example through carbon pricing or a need to buy more renewable energy [0000002488-26-000018:0050]. It adds that its manufacturing suppliers may face higher costs from new climate-related regulations affecting abatement equipment, renewable energy, production processes and material choices [0000002488-26-000018:0050].
The NVIDIA excerpts concern export controls and related government restrictions, not environmental or climate regulation [0001045810-26-000021:0041][0001045810-26-000021:0044]. The Intel excerpts concern the cost and risk of process nodes, dependence on TSMC, and the Intel 14A foundry decision, not environmental or climate regulation [0000050863-26-000011:0063][0000050863-26-000011:0065].

questions.question: How does the share price shape the talent-retention risk that NVIDIA, AMD and Intel each describe in their latest 10-K risk factors?

answer.text:
NVIDIA says that in times of stock price volatility, as it has experienced in the past and may experience in the future, the retentive value of its stock-based compensation may decrease [0001045810-26-000021:0037]. It adds that competition for talent drives up costs in the form of cash and stock-based compensation [0001045810-26-000021:0037].
AMD says it uses share-based incentive awards to help attract, retain and motivate executives and qualified employees [0000002488-26-000018:0060]. If the value of those awards does not appreciate with its stock price, or if share-based compensation ceases to be viewed as a valuable benefit, its ability to attract, retain and motivate employees could be affected, which could harm its results of operations [0000002488-26-000018:0060]. AMD also says that if the value of its stock awards increases substantially, this could create great personal wealth for executives and key talent and affect its ability to retain them [0000002488-26-000018:0060]. AMD adds that stock price fluctuations could affect the value of its equity compensation and thus its ability to recruit and retain employees [0000002488-26-000018:0061].
Intel says it uses share-based awards, such as RSUs, and performance-based cash incentive awards to help attract, retain and motivate qualified employees [0000050863-26-000011:0082]. It states that sustained declines in its stock price, or lower stock price performance relative to competitors in recent years, have reduced the retention value of its share-based awards, which has impacted the competitiveness of its compensation [0000050863-26-000011:0082].

questions.question: How did AI accelerator demand show up in each company's segment results in its latest 10-K, and what accelerator-related inventory charges offset it?

answer.text:
AMD's Data Center net revenue was $16.6 billion in 2025, up 32% from $12.6 billion in 2024, driven primarily by strong demand for AMD EPYC processors and AMD Instinct GPU accelerators [0000002488-26-000018:0076]. Data Center operating income was $3,603 million in 2025 against $3,482 million in 2024 [0000002488-26-000018:0076]. AMD said demand for its data center AI GPU products was strong as large hyperscale customers, OEMs and ODMs deployed AMD Instinct MI350X Series GPUs [0000002488-26-000018:0071].
AMD incurred approximately $800 million in inventory and related charges in the second quarter of 2025 as a result [0000002488-26-000018:0042]. After licenses were granted and shipments began in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025, AMD reversed approximately $360 million of those charges [0000002488-26-000018:0042].
It says Intel missed the significant shift in compute demand to GPUs optimized for AI workloads and has been unsuccessful to date in becoming a meaningful participant in that market [0000050863-26-000011:0062]. Its Gaudi AI accelerator effort was unsuccessful, and Intel recognized Gaudi AI accelerator inventory-related charges of $375 million in 2025 and $922 million in 2024 [0000050863-26-000011:0062].

questions.question: How do NVIDIA, AMD and Intel each address the OECD Pillar Two global minimum tax in their latest 10-Ks, and has any of them quantified its impact?

answer.text:
AMD says the OECD is continuing discussions on changes to how profits are allocated among tax jurisdictions and on a global minimum tax under "Pillar One" and "Pillar Two" [0000002488-26-000018:0079]. It notes that the Council of the European Union has adopted the 15% global minimum tax in Pillar Two and has directed EU member states to legislate it [0000002488-26-000018:0079]. Many countries, including non-EU states, have implemented Pillar Two-based laws with effective dates starting in 2024, but certain jurisdictions where AMD operates have not yet adopted corresponding legislation [0000002488-26-000018:0079]. AMD also says that in January 2026 the OECD released a "side-by-side" package with new safe harbors and an exemption for U.S.-based multinationals from parts of the global minimum tax framework [0000002488-26-000018:0079]. In its risk factors, AMD calls these rules generally favorable to the Company but says each country must adopt them before they count as enacted for financial accounting purposes [0000002488-26-000018:0046]. AMD says it will keep evaluating the effect on its effective tax rate and cash flows as new guidance emerges [0000002488-26-000018:0079][0000002488-26-000018:0046].
AMD is the only one of the three to characterize the impact, and it does so qualitatively: it says the impact of Pillar Two was immaterial for 2024 and 2025 [0000002488-26-000018:0079]. It gives no dollar figure for that impact [0000002488-26-000018:0079].
They show only that NVIDIA's income tax expense was $21,383 million for the fiscal year ended Jan 25, 2026 [0001045810-26-000021:0088]. They attribute Intel's 2025 effective tax rate of 98.3% mainly to a change in valuation allowance against current-year tax attributes, offset by the nonrecurring gain on the Altera divestiture [0000050863-26-000011:0046].

questions.question: How does dependence on external foundries, and on TSMC in particular, differ across NVIDIA, AMD and Intel according to their latest 10-K risk factors?

answer.text:
The NVIDIA excerpt covers U.S. export controls and says nothing about foundry or TSMC dependence, so no NVIDIA comparison can be drawn [0001045810-26-000021:0044].
AMD says it uses third-party wafer foundries to fabricate the silicon wafers for all of its products [0000002488-26-000018:0029]. It relies on TSMC for all wafers for microprocessor and GPU products at 7 nm or smaller nodes, and primarily on GLOBALFOUNDRIES (GF) for those products at nodes larger than 7 nm [0000002488-26-000018:0029]. AMD states that if TSMC cannot make wafers at 7 nm or smaller nodes in sufficient quantities, it could have a material adverse effect on its business [0000002488-26-000018:0032]. It also notes that TSMC manufactures its newest IC products [0000002488-26-000018:0032]. AMD adds that it lacks long-term commitment contracts with some manufacturing suppliers and obtains many services on a purchase order basis [0000002488-26-000018:0029]. Those manufacturers also serve other companies, including certain AMD competitors, and could prioritize other customers' capacity, raise prices on short notice, require onerous prepayments, or cut deliveries [0000002488-26-000018:0029]. AMD has a wafer supply agreement with GF that sets a minimum annual capacity allocation and pricing through 2026 [0000002488-26-000018:0029].
It plans to keep manufacturing the majority of its products in its own factories [0000050863-26-000011:0008]. It also uses third-party foundry capacity, including at TSMC, for various tiles or entire products, and expects to keep using TSMC and other suppliers for key tiles in a number of current and future products [0000050863-26-000011:0018]. Intel describes TSMC as a key competitor on the foundry side of its business [0000050863-26-000011:0063]. Intel states that if TSMC supply of tiles were interrupted, whether through a dispute or otherwise, it could not complete products requiring those tiles until it designed and sourced replacements, which would likely involve a substantial delay [0000050863-26-000011:0063]. Intel calls its disaggregated design approach a significant supply chain risk [0000050863-26-000011:0063].
If it cannot secure a significant external foundry customer for Intel 14A, it may pause or discontinue Intel 14A and successor nodes, and would expect over time to shift manufacturing to third-party foundries, particularly TSMC [0000050863-26-000011:0008]. In that case it would have no long-term contract with TSMC, and most of its competitors have longer and more established relationships with TSMC and other third-party foundries [0000050863-26-000011:0065]. Intel says only TSMC and Samsung are currently capable of producing the leading-edge and near-leading-edge nodes its products need [0000050863-26-000011:0065].

questions.question: How concentrated is each company's revenue among its largest customers, as disclosed in the latest 10-K risk factors of NVIDIA, AMD and Intel?

answer.text:
NVIDIA: For fiscal year 2026, sales to one direct customer represented 22% of total revenue and sales to another direct customer represented 14% of total revenue, all primarily attributable to the Compute & Networking segment [0001045810-26-000021:0036]. NVIDIA also says it generates a significant amount of revenue from a limited number of indirect customers, and it estimates that some of them individually represent 10% or more of its revenue [0001045810-26-000021:0036].
Intel: Its three largest customers collectively accounted for 43% of net revenue in 2025, 45% in 2024 and 40% in 2023 [0000050863-26-000011:0083]. Intel expects a small number of customers to continue to account for a significant portion of its revenue in the foreseeable future [0000050863-26-000011:0084].
AMD: The risk factor says AMD depends on a small number of customers for a substantial portion of its business, and it expects a small number of customers to continue to account for a significant part of its revenue and receivables in the future [0000002488-26-000018:0026].

questions.question: How do NVIDIA, AMD and Intel each describe the role of their software and developer ecosystems in competing for AI and computing workloads, according to their latest 10-Ks?

answer.text:
NVIDIA says its technology stack includes the CUDA development platform that runs on all NVIDIA GPUs, along with hundreds of domain-specific software libraries, frameworks, algorithms, SDKs and APIs [0001045810-26-000021:0004]. It describes a platform strategy that combines hardware, systems, software, algorithms, libraries, AI models and training data sets, and services [0001045810-26-000021:0004]. NVIDIA says a unified programmable architecture lets it support several multi-billion-dollar end markets with the same underlying technology, using software stacks developed internally or by third parties [0001045810-26-000021:0004]. It adds that the large and growing number of developers and the installed base strengthen its ecosystem and raise the value of the platform for customers [0001045810-26-000021:0004].
NVIDIA reports over 7.5 million developers worldwide using CUDA and its other software tools, and says its computing platforms are available from virtually every major server maker and CSP [0001045810-26-000021:0009]. It also says more than half of its engineers work on software [0001045810-26-000021:0005]. NVIDIA offers NVIDIA AI Enterprise, a software suite for developing and deploying production-grade generative AI applications [0001045810-26-000021:0009]. It also sells paid licenses to NVIDIA AI Enterprise and NVIDIA vGPU software [0001045810-26-000021:0007].
AMD says it has a comprehensive and open AI software stack to support diverse AI ecosystems across frameworks, large and small language models, and applications [0000002488-26-000018:0005]. It says it continues to invest in software capabilities and the open ecosystem through the AMD ROCm platform, which delivers new features for AI training and inference [0000002488-26-000018:0005]. In 2025, AMD introduced key optimizations and expanded support for frameworks and libraries, improving generative AI performance and simplifying the developer experience [0000002488-26-000018:0005]. To execute its AI strategy, AMD brought in multiple AI teams to develop a comprehensive software ecosystem spanning its full product portfolio [0000002488-26-000018:0071]. It also made acquisitions to add software capabilities, including compiler and AI expertise in machine learning, inference and performance optimization [0000002488-26-000018:0071]. For its adaptable platforms, AMD offers the Vivado Design Suite, the Vitis unified software platform and the Vitis AI platform for FPGAs and adaptive SoCs [0000002488-26-000018:0011].

questions.question: How do NVIDIA, AMD and Intel each characterise the risk of third-party intellectual property infringement claims in their latest 10-Ks, and which of them points to non-practicing entities?

answer.text:
Intel says third parties assert IP claims against it and its products, which could harm its business, and that it faces claims from individuals, companies, investment litigation entities, other non-practicing entities, and academic and research institutions [0000050863-26-000011:0080]. Intel reports an increase in patent assertions and lawsuits from well-funded non-practicing entities, including entities funded by third-party investment firms [0000050863-26-000011:0080]. It also names the VLSI and R2 litigation as having resulted in significant adverse judgments and settlements [0000050863-26-000011:0080]. Intel says it is typically engaged in a number of IP disputes, and that such claims, regardless of merit, cause large costs and divert management and technical attention [0000050863-26-000011:0080]. Possible consequences include paying damages, stopping the manufacture or sale of affected products, developing alternative technology, or entering into licences that may not be available on reasonable terms [0000050863-26-000011:0080].
NVIDIA says it is involved from time to time in lawsuits or legal proceedings alleging patent infringement or other IP violations by it, its employees or parties it has agreed to indemnify [0001045810-26-000021:0047]. It says an unfavorable ruling could bring significant damages, patent invalidation, indemnification of third parties, payment of lost profits, or injunctive relief [0001045810-26-000021:0047]. It adds that infringement claims, regardless of merit, could cause significant costs and divert management and technical personnel [0001045810-26-000021:0047]. For AMD, the excerpts include a risk-summary bullet on protecting its own technology and IP, and a bullet saying its ability to design and introduce new products includes the use of third-party IP [0000002488-26-000018:0021]. Its litigation risk factor says it is a defendant or plaintiff in various legal actions and that a successful claim could lead to material damages [0000002488-26-000018:0047].

questions.question: According to NVIDIA's FY2026 10-K, how have U.S. export controls affected demand for NVIDIA products outside China, and what has the Chinese government done to discourage purchases of its data center products?

answer.text:
Outside China: The 10-K says export controls have in the past and may in the future negatively impact demand for NVIDIA's products and services not only in China but also in markets such as Europe, Latin America, and Southeast Asia [0001045810-26-000021:0045]. It says the possibility of additional export controls has negatively impacted, and may in the future negatively impact, demand for its products, benefiting competitors that offer alternatives less likely to be restricted [0001045810-26-000021:0041]. Export controls have already encouraged, and may continue to encourage, customers outside China and other impacted regions to "design-out" certain U.S. semiconductors from their products [0001045810-26-000021:0045]. They have also encouraged overseas governments to ask NVIDIA's customers to buy from competitors rather than NVIDIA or other U.S. firms [0001045810-26-000021:0045]. The licensing requirements may encourage customers in China, the Middle East, and other regions to pursue alternatives, including semiconductor suppliers based in China, Europe, and Israel [0001045810-26-000021:0043]. Export controls can also disrupt NVIDIA's supply chain and distribution channels, hurting its ability to serve demand in markets outside China and for its non-data center products [0001045810-26-000021:0041]. Restrictions on data center GPUs may also reduce demand for NVIDIA's networking products used in servers containing those GPUs [0001045810-26-000021:0044]. Reduced demand due to export controls has led and could lead to excess inventory or related supply charges [0001045810-26-000021:0041].
Chinese government actions: The Chinese government has encouraged customers to purchase from China-based competitors and discouraged them from purchasing, importing, or using NVIDIA's data center products, including any China-specific product designed to comply with U.S. export controls [0001045810-26-000021:0045]. After U.S. legislative proposals calling for mandatory features in NVIDIA's chips, China's government publicly questioned whether the H20 products have built-in vulnerabilities, discouraging customers from purchasing them [0001045810-26-000021:0044]. An agency of the Chinese government announced an Action Plan endorsing new standards on compute performance per watt and per memory bandwidth for accelerators in new and renovated data centers, which could restrict customers' use of some NVIDIA data center products if NVIDIA returned to the market [0001045810-26-000021:0045]. On September 15, 2025, China's antitrust regulators published a preliminary finding that NVIDIA's compliance with U.S. export controls, which required offering degraded products to the Chinese market, discriminated unfairly against customers in China and violated the terms of China's approval of the Mellanox acquisition [0001045810-26-000021:0041].

questions.question: What is the status of NVIDIA's licensed H20 and H200 sales to China as described in its FY2026 10-K, including the financial impact and conditions attached to the licenses?

answer.text:
In April 2025, the USG informed NVIDIA that it requires a license for export to China (including Hong Kong and Macau) and D:5 countries, or to companies headquartered or with an ultimate parent therein, of its H20 integrated circuits and any other circuits achieving the H20's memory bandwidth, interconnect bandwidth, or combination thereof [0001045810-26-000021:0042]. As a result, NVIDIA incurred a $4.5 billion charge in the first quarter of fiscal year 2026 associated with H20 for excess inventory and purchase obligations, as demand for H20 products diminished [0001045810-26-000021:0042][0001045810-26-000021:0061].
In August 2025, the USG granted licenses that would allow NVIDIA to ship certain H20 products to certain China-based customers, and NVIDIA generated approximately $60 million in H20 revenue under those licenses [0001045810-26-000021:0042][0001045810-26-000021:0061]. USG officials expressed an expectation that the USG will receive 15% or more of the revenue generated from licensed sales of NVIDIA's products, but the USG did not publish a regulation codifying such requirement [0001045810-26-000021:0042].
In February 2026, the USG granted a license that would allow NVIDIA to ship small amounts of H200 products to specific China-based customers [0001045810-26-000021:0042]. To date, NVIDIA has not generated any revenue under the H200 licensing program and does not yet know whether any imports will be allowed into China [0001045810-26-000021:0042][0001045810-26-000021:0061]. The license requires that the H200s go through an inspection process in the United States prior to any shipment to the customer, so any H200 shipped under the program will be subject to a 25% tariff upon importation into the United States [0001045810-26-000021:0042][0001045810-26-000021:0061].
If NVIDIA is able to sell licensed products into the China market, it may not be able to pass along all or any of the tariff to its customers, and may be subject to litigation, increased costs, and a harmed competitive position [0001045810-26-000021:0042]. NVIDIA also states that, as of the end of fiscal year 2026, it was effectively foreclosed from competing in China's data center computing market [0001045810-26-000021:0042].

questions.question: How concentrated was NVIDIA's revenue among direct customers in fiscal year 2026, and what risks does NVIDIA associate with that concentration?

answer.text:
For fiscal year 2026, sales to one direct customer represented 22% of NVIDIA's total revenue and sales to another direct customer represented 14%, all of which were primarily attributable to the Compute & Networking segment [0001045810-26-000021:0067][0001045810-26-000021:0125]. In fiscal year 2025, one direct customer represented 12% of total revenue and two others each represented 11%, and in fiscal year 2024 one direct customer represented 13% [0001045810-26-000021:0067]. NVIDIA states that its revenue is concentrated among a limited number of direct and indirect customers and that this trend may continue [0001045810-26-000021:0067].
On indirect customers, NVIDIA says it generates a significant amount of revenue from a limited number of them, some individually representing 10% or more of revenue [0001045810-26-000021:0036].
The risk factor says revenue could be adversely affected if NVIDIA loses or is prevented from selling to any of these customers [0001045810-26-000021:0036]. Most sales are made on a purchase order basis, so customers can generally cancel, change or delay purchase commitments with little notice and without penalty [0001045810-26-000021:0036]. Partners or customers may buy fewer products, decline to incorporate NVIDIA's products into their ecosystem, develop their own solutions, or buy from competitors [0001045810-26-000021:0036]. NVIDIA also notes that a small number of partners are involved in system integration with its key customers, and that as system designs grow more complex, system integrators may be unable to meet key customers' specifications [0001045810-26-000021:0036]. If end demand rises or finished goods supply is concentrated near a quarter end, system integrators, distributors and channel partners may have limited ability to increase their credit, which could affect the timing and amount of revenue [0001045810-26-000021:0036]. Finally, NVIDIA says that the loss of any large customer, a significant reduction in their purchases, an inability to sell to a customer because of U.S. or other countries' trade restrictions, or difficulties collecting accounts receivable would likely harm its financial condition and results of operations [0001045810-26-000021:0036].

questions.question: What drove growth in NVIDIA's Compute & Networking segment in the first nine months of fiscal year 2026, broken down between Data Center computing and networking?

answer.text: The filing says the year-over-year increase in Compute & Networking revenue in the third quarter and first nine months of fiscal year 2026 was driven by three platform shifts: accelerated computing, powerful AI models, and agentic applications [0001045810-25-000230:0040]. Data Center computing revenue grew 59% year-on-year compared to the first nine months of fiscal year 2025, driven by demand for the Blackwell computing platform [0001045810-25-000230:0040]. Data Center networking revenue grew 105% year-on-year over the same period, driven by the introduction and continued growth of NVLink compute fabric for GB200 and GB300 systems, the growth of XDR InfiniBand products, and adoption of Ethernet for AI solutions [0001045810-25-000230:0040].

questions.question: In its Q3 fiscal 2026 10-Q, how does NVIDIA say export controls could affect its gaming and networking products beyond data center GPUs?

answer.text:
On gaming, NVIDIA says the USG already imposed export controls restricting certain gaming GPUs, and that expanding them to additional gaming products may disrupt a significant portion of its supply and distribution chain and negatively impact sales of such products to markets outside China, including the U.S. and Europe [0001045810-25-000230:0063]. It adds that as gaming GPU performance increases over time, export controls may have a greater impact on its ability to compete in markets subject to those controls [0001045810-25-000230:0063]. It also notes that export controls may disrupt the supply and distribution chain for a substantial portion of its products, which are warehoused in and distributed from Hong Kong [0001045810-25-000230:0063]. Separately, it says export controls have disrupted and could in the future disrupt its supply chain and distribution channels, affecting its ability to serve demand in markets outside China and for its non-data center products [0001045810-25-000230:0059]. Restrictions by the Chinese government on the duration of gaming activities and access to games may also adversely affect Gaming revenue [0001045810-25-000230:0064].
On networking, NVIDIA says export controls restricting its ability to sell data center GPUs may also negatively impact demand for its networking products used in servers containing its GPUs [0001045810-25-000230:0063]. It says the USG may also impose export controls on networking products, such as high-speed network interconnects, to limit the ability of downstream parties to create large clusters for frontier model training [0001045810-25-000230:0063]. In addition, China's antitrust regulators published a preliminary finding on September 15, 2025 that NVIDIA's compliance with U.S. export controls violated the terms of China's approval of the Mellanox acquisition, and if regulators conclude NVIDIA failed to fulfill those terms, it could face restrictions or other orders regarding its networking business, products, and services [0001045810-25-000230:0060].

questions.question: How did the April 2025 U.S. export license requirement affect AMD's MI308 business over fiscal 2025, according to AMD's FY2025 10-K?

answer.text: In April 2025, the U.S. government implemented a new license requirement for the export of certain semiconductor products to a D5 Country and to companies headquartered in, or with an ultimate parent in, such a country, and this restriction impacts AMD's Instinct MI308 products [0000002488-26-000018:0042]. As a result, AMD incurred approximately $800 million in inventory and related charges in the second quarter of 2025 [0000002488-26-000018:0042][0000002488-26-000018:0072]. AMD applied for and was granted some licenses that allow it to ship MI308 products to certain China-based customers [0000002488-26-000018:0042]. During the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025, AMD began shipping products and reversed approximately $360 million of the charges recorded earlier in the year [0000002488-26-000018:0042][0000002488-26-000018:0072]. The net effect for the year was approximately $440 million of net inventory and related charges associated with the export control on MI308 products, which partially offset the gross margin improvement to 50% from 49% in 2024 [0000002488-26-000018:0070][0000002488-26-000018:0078]. The same $440 million of net charges also partially offset the increase in Data Center operating income, which was $3.6 billion in 2025 versus $3.5 billion in 2024 [0000002488-26-000018:0077]. AMD states that sales of MI308 products into China depend on customer demand, China's import control rules and its ability to obtain licenses [0000002488-26-000018:0042]. In August 2025, U.S. government officials expressed an expectation that the U.S. government will receive 15% of the revenue from licensed MI308 sales to China, but the government has not published a regulation establishing such a requirement [0000002488-26-000018:0042][0000002488-26-000018:0072].

questions.question: Which manufacturers does AMD rely on to produce its products, per its FY2025 10-K, and what supply risks does it describe from that reliance?

answer.text:
AMD uses third-party wafer foundries to fabricate the silicon wafers for all of its products [0000002488-26-000018:0029]. It relies on TSMC for all wafers for microprocessor and GPU products at 7 nm or smaller nodes, and primarily on GLOBALFOUNDRIES (GF) for microprocessor and GPU wafers at process nodes larger than 7 nm [0000002488-26-000018:0029]. It also uses TSMC, UMC and Samsung for its programmable logic device ICs [0000002488-26-000018:0029]. Third-party manufacturers assemble, test, mark and pack (ATMP) its products, and most ATMP services come from two ATMP joint ventures with affiliates of Tongfu Microelectronics Co., Ltd. [0000002488-26-000018:0029][0000002488-26-000018:0030].
- If it experiences supply constraints, AMD may have to allocate reduced quantities among customers, which could harm customer relationships and its financial condition [0000002488-26-000018:0029]. Late or fluctuating supply could cause lost sales [0000002488-26-000018:0029].
- If TSMC cannot make enough wafers at 7 nm or smaller nodes to meet demand, its business could be materially adversely affected [0000002488-26-000018:0029].
- AMD does not have long-term commitment contracts with some manufacturing suppliers, and obtains many services by purchase order with no minimum quantity beyond existing orders [0000002488-26-000018:0029]. Its manufacturers also serve other companies, including competitors, and could prioritize other customers' capacity, raise prices on short notice, require onerous prepayments, or reduce or eliminate deliveries [0000002488-26-000018:0029].
- Under its wafer supply agreement with GF, which sets a minimum annual capacity allocation and pricing through 2026, AMD could face excess inventory or higher inventory unit costs if its wafer requirements fall below the annual purchase target [0000002488-26-000018:0030].
- Other risks include limited control over delivery schedules, yield, cycle times, quality assurance and price increases, as well as supply disruptions at manufacturers or their subcontractors [0000002488-26-000018:0030]. AMD cites inventory loss from an incident at a contract manufacturer in the first quarter of 2024 [0000002488-26-000018:0030].
- Moving production to new manufacturers could cause delayed product introductions, lower yields or poorer performance, and finding alternative manufacturers could cause significant shipment delays [0000002488-26-000018:0030].
- There is no guarantee that the ATMP JVs can fulfill AMD's long-term ATMP requirements [0000002488-26-000018:0030].
- Manufacturing inefficiencies or disruptions could lead to unacceptable yields or product delivery delays [0000002488-26-000018:0032]. Lower yields could raise per-unit costs, hurt gross margin, or force AMD to allocate reduced supply among customers [0000002488-26-000018:0032].
- Certain equipment and materials come from a limited number of suppliers, or a sole supplier, and AMD notes an industry-wide memory shortage that has raised memory prices [0000002488-26-000018:0031].

- Moving production to new manufacturers could cause delayed product introductions, lower yields or poorer performance, and finding alternative manufacturers could cause significant shipment delays [0000002488-26-000018:0030].

- Manufacturing inefficiencies or disruptions could lead to unacceptable yields or product delivery delays [0000002488-26-000018:0032].
Lower yields could raise per-unit costs, hurt gross margin, or force AMD to allocate reduced supply among customers [0000002488-26-000018:0032].

questions.question: What drove AMD's Data Center segment revenue and operating income in 2025, according to its FY2025 10-K MD&A?

answer.text:
Data Center net revenue was $16.6 billion in 2025, up 32% from $12.6 billion in 2024, and the increase was primarily driven by strong demand for AMD EPYC processors and AMD Instinct GPU accelerators [0000002488-26-000018:0077]. The MD&A overview more specifically attributes the growth to strong demand for 5th generation AMD EPYC processors and AMD Instinct MI350 Series GPUs [0000002488-26-000018:0070].
Data Center operating income was $3.6 billion in 2025, compared with $3.5 billion in 2024 [0000002488-26-000018:0077]. questions.question: How did AMD change its segment reporting in fiscal 2025, and what drove the growth of the Client and Gaming segment that year?

answer.text:
Beginning with the fiscal year ending December 27, 2025, AMD combined its Client and Gaming segments into one reportable segment to align with how it manages its business [0000002488-25-000047:0023][0000002488-25-000166:0031]. Neither Client nor Gaming qualifies as a separate reportable operating segment, but AMD still discloses revenue for each business separately, and all prior period segment data were retrospectively adjusted [0000002488-25-000047:0023][0000002488-25-000166:0031].
Client and Gaming net revenue was $14.6 billion in 2025, up 51% from $9.6 billion in 2024 [0000002488-26-000018:0077]. Client net revenue of $10.6 billion increased 51%, primarily driven by a 31% increase in unit shipments of processors and a 15% increase in average selling price of processors, reflecting strong demand for AMD desktop and mobile Ryzen processors [0000002488-26-000018:0077]. Gaming net revenue of $3.9 billion increased 51%, primarily driven by higher semi-custom revenue and strong demand for Radeon gaming GPUs [0000002488-26-000018:0077].
Client and Gaming operating income rose to $2.9 billion in 2025 from $1.2 billion in 2024, primarily driven by higher revenue, partially offset by higher cost of sales and operating expenses [0000002488-26-000018:0077].

questions.question: What were AMD's main product and AI strategy milestones in 2025, as described in the FY2025 10-K MD&A?

answer.text:
AMD said a priority in 2025 was accelerating growth in the Data Center segment, where demand for its data center AI GPU products was strong as large hyperscale customers, OEMs and ODMs deployed AMD Instinct MI350X Series GPUs [0000002488-26-000018:0071]. It advanced its AMD AI GPU roadmap toward an annual cadence of leadership for AMD Instinct solutions, beginning with the MI350 Series GPUs in 2025 [0000002488-26-000018:0071].
Beyond GPUs, AMD launched the 5th Gen AMD EPYC family of server processors in 2025 [0000002488-26-000018:0071]. It expanded its data center portfolio with new networking solutions, including the AMD Pensando "Pollara" 400 AI NICs and "Vulcano" AI NICs [0000002488-26-000018:0071]. It also previewed its Helios AI rack-scale platform, which incorporates all of its data center products (CPUs, GPUs and networking) [0000002488-26-000018:0071].
In Client and Gaming, AMD brought to market AMD Radeon 9000 Series GPUs and Radeon AI PRO 9700 GPUs based on the AMD RDNA 4 graphics architecture, along with new Ryzen Threadripper 9000 Series processors [0000002488-26-000018:0071]. In its x86 Embedded portfolio, it introduced three new AMD EPYC embedded processor series: EPYC Embedded 9005, 4005 and 2005 [0000002488-26-000018:0071].
AMD also made strategic acquisitions to advance its software capabilities, including compiler and AI expertise, to scale its photonics and co-packaged optics solutions, and to add expertise in high-speed inference and reasoning-based AI technologies [0000002488-26-000018:0071]. It brought in multiple AI teams to develop a comprehensive software ecosystem, and delivered optimizations and expanded framework and library support in the latest version of AMD ROCm software [0000002488-26-000018:0071].
The MD&A also reports that net revenue rose 34% to $34.6 billion in 2025, from $25.8 billion in 2024 [0000002488-26-000018:0070]. Data Center net revenue was $16.6 billion, up 32%, and Client and Gaming net revenue was $14.6 billion, up 51% [0000002488-26-000018:0070].

questions.question: What happened with AMD's acquisition of ZT Systems during fiscal 2025, including the subsequent divestiture of its manufacturing business?

answer.text:
AMD completed the acquisition of ZT Systems on March 31, 2025, paying $3.2 billion in cash and issuing 8,335,849 shares of its common stock on the Acquisition Date [0000002488-25-000166:0030]. The total purchase consideration was $4.4 billion, made up of $3,188 million of cash, $860 million fair value of shares issued and $361 million fair value of contingent consideration not yet paid [0000002488-25-000166:0014]. The company said the acquisition is expected to enable AMD to deliver end-to-end AI solutions and accelerate the design and deployment of AMD-powered AI infrastructure at scale [0000002488-25-000166:0030].
AMD had disclosed in August 2024 its intent to divest ZT Systems' data center infrastructure manufacturing business (the ZT Manufacturing Business), keeping only certain intellectual property and employees (the ZT Design Business) [0000002488-25-000108:0030]. On acquisition, it classified the manufacturing business and its related assets and liabilities as held for sale [0000002488-25-000108:0030]. The manufacturing business's results are presented in discontinued operations, while the design business's results are in continuing operations within the Data Center segment and are not material [0000002488-25-000166:0014].
On May 18, 2025, AMD entered into an equity purchase agreement with Sanmina Corporation to sell the ZT Manufacturing Business for $3.0 billion in cash and stock, inclusive of a contingent payment of up to $450 million [0000002488-25-000108:0038]. The agreement provided for a termination fee of up to $153 million if the sale was not completed by May 18, 2026, subject to two automatic extensions until November 18, 2026 [0000002488-25-000108:0030].
On October 27, 2025, AMD completed the sale to Sanmina for 1,151,052 shares of Sanmina common stock and $2.4 billion in cash, subject to certain purchase price adjustments, and it is eligible for up to $450 million of additional cash consideration if certain conditions are met after closing [0000002488-25-000166:0030]. Sanmina will also be AMD's preferred partner for manufacturing capabilities in building complex AI solutions [0000002488-26-000018:0072].
On October 30, 2025, AMD settled the contingent consideration liability with the former ZT Systems stockholders and warrant holders for $300 million in cash and 740,961 shares of AMD common stock [0000002488-25-000166:0030].

questions.question: What caused the declines in AMD's Gaming and Embedded segment revenue in fiscal 2024?

answer.text:
AMD's Gaming net revenue was $2.6 billion in 2024, down 58% from $6.2 billion in 2023, and the 10-K attributes the decrease primarily to lower semi-custom product revenue [0000002488-25-000012:0074]. For Q2 2024, Gaming revenue fell 59% and for the six months it fell 53%, both primarily due to lower semi-custom revenue [0000002488-24-000123:0027]. For the nine months ended September 28, 2024, Gaming revenue fell 58%, again primarily due to lower semi-custom revenue [0000002488-24-000163:0027]. In Q1 2024, Gaming revenue fell 48%, primarily due to a decrease in semi-custom revenue and lower Radeon GPU sales [0000002488-24-000056:0023].
The 10-K attributes the decrease primarily to lower demand as customers continued to normalize their inventory levels [0000002488-25-000012:0074]. In Q1 2024, Embedded revenue fell 46% as customers continued to manage their inventory levels [0000002488-24-000056:0023]. In Q2 2024, the decrease was primarily due to customers continuing to normalize their inventory levels [0000002488-24-000123:0027]. For the three and nine months ended September 28, 2024, revenue decreased as customers continued to normalize their inventory levels [0000002488-24-000163:0027].

questions.question: How does AMD's FY2025 10-K describe the status of the AI Diffusion Rule and the risks from potential replacement export rules and tariffs?

answer.text:
AMD's FY2025 10-K says that in January 2025 BIS issued a final rule, commonly referred to as the "AI Diffusion Rule," that would have imposed new restrictions on the export, reexport and in-country transfer of certain advanced semiconductor devices and technology [0000002488-26-000018:0043]. In May 2025, BIS announced its intention to rescind the rule, publish a regulation formalizing the rescission, and issue replacement rules in the future [0000002488-26-000018:0043].
On the replacement rules, AMD says they may limit its ability to engage in certain business transactions, require new export licenses, delay shipments, or necessitate changes in compliance processes and product designs [0000002488-26-000018:0043]. BIS's announced plans also create uncertainty over whether specific products, technologies or software fall within the scope of any new restrictions, and over whether BIS will grant licenses in a timely manner or at all [0000002488-26-000018:0043]. AMD adds that compliance with planned or existing rules could result in increased costs, disruption of key customer and supplier relationships, loss of competitive positioning in international markets or reputational harm [0000002488-26-000018:0043].
On tariffs, AMD says the U.S. government has instituted or proposed changes in trade policies, including higher tariffs on imports into the U.S., which could significantly impact its business, particularly the import of products manufactured outside the U.S. [0000002488-26-000018:0043]. Retaliatory actions by foreign governments could result in tariffs, trade protection measures or other restrictions on AMD's current and future products [0000002488-26-000018:0043]. Customer demand could then decline, which could hurt revenue and result in inventory impairment charges [0000002488-26-000018:0044]. For example, tariffs on hardware required for data centers could raise costs for customers, potentially causing them to delay or cancel AI infrastructure investments [0000002488-26-000018:0044].

questions.question: How did Intel change its approach to deploying manufacturing capital in 2025, and what does its FY2025 10-K say would happen to Intel 14A if it cannot secure a significant external customer?

answer.text:
In 2025, Intel streamlined its footprint to improve operational efficiency and better align capacity with anticipated demand [0000050863-26-000011:0008]. It initiated the consolidation of its Costa Rican assembly and test operations into larger existing sites in Vietnam and Malaysia, slowed the pace of construction for its new Ohio fab, and discontinued planned expansions in Germany (fab) and Poland (assembly and test) to better align capital spending with market demand [0000050863-26-000011:0034]. The filing says these actions reflect a focus on deploying capital in coordination with tangible milestones and scaling capacity as needed [0000050863-26-000011:0034]. Intel also says it will only deploy capital on new nodes and manufacturing facilities where it believes they will yield an attractive return [0000050863-26-000011:0034]. It expects the Costa Rica consolidation to be completed by the end of 2026 [0000050863-26-000011:0008].
On Intel 14A, the filing says that if Intel is unable to secure a significant external customer and meet important customer milestones, it faces the prospect that it will not be economical to develop and manufacture Intel 14A and successor leading-edge nodes on a go-forward basis [0000050863-26-000011:0034]. In that event, it may pause or discontinue its pursuit of Intel 14A and successor nodes and various of its manufacturing expansion projects [0000050863-26-000011:0034]. Intel would expect, over time, to shift manufacturing to third-party foundries, particularly TSMC, as it develops products for nodes beyond Intel 18A and Intel 18A-P [0000050863-26-000011:0008]. If it discontinued Intel 14A and successor nodes, it expects a majority of its products would continue to be manufactured in its own facilities using nodes up to Intel 18A-P through at least 2030 [0000050863-26-000011:0034].

questions.question: What were the key terms of Intel's August 2025 agreement with the U.S. Department of Commerce, as described in its FY2025 10-K?

answer.text:
On August 22, 2025, Intel entered into a Warrant and Common Stock Agreement (the U.S. Government Agreement) with the U.S. Department of Commerce (DOC) to support the continued expansion of U.S. semiconductor technology and manufacturing leadership [0000050863-26-000011:0030]. On August 27, 2025, Intel amended its commercial CHIPS Act agreement with the DOC, removing the prior project milestone requirements and other conditions to disbursements, as well as substantially all other requirements other than those required by law, including those tied to the $2.3 billion previously received and recognized as government incentives [0000050863-26-000011:0030]. Intel received the full $5.7 billion of accelerated disbursements remaining under the commercial CHIPS Act agreement [0000050863-26-000011:0030].
Intel issued to the DOC 275 million shares of its common stock and a warrant to purchase up to 241 million shares at $20.00 per share if Intel were to cease to directly or indirectly own at least 51% of its Intel Foundry business [0000050863-26-000011:0030]. Intel also issued 159 million shares into escrow, to be released to the U.S. government on a $20.00 per share basis as Intel receives the $3.2 billion of disbursements contemplated under the Secure Enclave program of the CHIPS Act [0000050863-26-000011:0030]. As of December 27, 2025, Intel had released 3 million Escrowed Shares upon receipt of cash proceeds for its Secure Enclave performance [0000050863-26-000011:0030].
If Escrowed Shares are not released from escrow at the end of the performance period, half will be released to the DOC with no consideration and the other half will be forfeited and cancelled [0000050863-26-000011:0180].
Intel's accounting conclusion for the agreement was adjusted after consultation with the SEC staff, which concluded in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025, after the Q3 2025 Form 10-Q was filed on November 6, 2025; Intel concluded the adjustments were immaterial to the Q3 2025 financial statements [0000050863-26-000011:0030]. In 2025, Intel recorded a $1.8 billion net loss from the change in fair value of the derivative liability for the Escrowed Shares [0000050863-26-000011:0046].

questions.question: What did Intel's 2025 Restructuring Plan aim to do, and what restructuring and related charges did Intel record in 2025?

answer.text:
Intel's 2025 Restructuring Plan was intended to lower expenses, streamline the organizational structure and reduce management layers across functions, while reallocating resources toward the core client and server businesses by reducing lower-priority programs and initiatives [0000050863-26-000011:0135].
The headcount reduction initiatives reduced Intel's core workforce by approximately 15% by the end of fiscal 2025, compared with the Q2 2025 ending headcount [0000050863-26-000011:0032].
In 2025, Intel recognized restructuring charges of $2.2 billion, consisting primarily of charges from initiating and deploying the 2025 Restructuring Plan and from substantially completing the 2024 Restructuring Plan [0000050863-26-000011:0032].
These charges were primarily cash-based employee severance and related employee exit charges of $1.8 billion and non-cash asset impairment charges of $474 million, resulting from the exit of certain non-core lines of business and the consolidation and exit of certain real estate properties [0000050863-26-000011:0032].
The cumulative cost of the 2025 Restructuring Plan as of December 27, 2025 was $2.0 billion, and Intel expects total charges of approximately $2.2 billion under the plan [0000050863-26-000011:0135].
Employee severance and benefit charges in 2025 included net charges of $1.5 billion under the 2025 Restructuring Plan and $281 million for the 2024 Restructuring Plan and other actions [0000050863-26-000011:0135].
Separately, Intel recorded non-cash accelerated depreciation and impairment charges of $950 million, net of certain items, to cost of sales in 2025 for certain manufacturing assets with no remaining operational use, which affected the Intel Foundry segment [0000050863-26-000011:0032].
A substantial majority of the plan's actions were completed in the fourth quarter of 2025, with the remainder expected in 2026 [0000050863-26-000011:0135].

questions.question: How did Intel describe Intel Foundry's strategy, process technology offerings and competitors in its FY2024 10-K?

answer.text:
Intel said Intel Foundry, which comprises technology development, manufacturing and foundry services, seeks to deliver the best systems foundry capabilities to support Intel Products and external customers [0000050863-25-000009:0030].
On strategy, Intel said it expects its manufacturing facilities to continue to mostly produce its own products for many years, while aiming to become a major provider of semiconductor manufacturing solutions for third parties as well [0000050863-25-000009:0030]. It said volume from its own products provides the scale required for leading-edge foundry operations and helps derisk the offerings for third-party customers [0000050863-25-000009:0030]. Third-party customers would add scale on the leading edge and, for mature nodes, allow better monetization of technology and manufacturing facility investments [0000050863-25-000009:0030]. Intel also plans to create greater independence for its foundry operations by establishing Intel Foundry as an independent subsidiary, which it expects to give clearer separation for foundry customers and suppliers and more flexibility to evaluate separate sources of funding and capital structures [0000050863-25-000009:0031]. Intel said it believes it is currently one of only three manufacturers pursuing 2nm lithography [0000050863-25-000009:0030].
On process technology, Intel said it expects to achieve volume production on its 2nm node, Intel 18A, in 2025 [0000050863-25-000009:0031]. The process technologies available to external customers are expected to include Intel 18A, featuring RibbonFET (gate-all-around) and PowerVia (back-side power delivery) as expected industry firsts [0000050863-25-000009:0031]. They also include the new Intel 3 process using EUV lithography, the established Intel 7 and Intel 16 processes, and a new 12nm process being developed in collaboration with UMC [0000050863-25-000009:0031]. Intel also announced an extension of its roadmap beyond Intel 18A with Intel 14A [0000050863-25-000009:0031]. Its advanced assembly and test offerings include technologies for packaging single chips or combining multiple chips adjacent to each other, stacked, or both [0000050863-25-000009:0031].
On competitors, Intel said Intel Foundry's competitors are primarily semiconductor foundries focused on wafers and packaging technologies from fabrication plants based primarily in Asia, including TSMC, Samsung, Global Foundries, UMC and SMIC [0000050863-25-000009:0031]. It said it competes with TSMC and Samsung in the advanced process technology marketplace [0000050863-25-000009:0031].

questions.question: Where does the European Commission competition case against Intel stand in its FY2025 10-K, and how much has Intel accrued for it?

answer.text:
In 2009 the EC found that Intel had used unfair business practices, and it imposed a €1.1 billion fine, which Intel paid in the third quarter of 2009 [0000050863-26-000011:0171]. In January 2022 the General Court annulled the EC's 2009 findings on rebates and the €1.1 billion fine, which was returned to Intel in February 2022 [0000050863-26-000011:0171]. The General Court did not annul the 2009 finding that Intel made payments to prevent sales of specific rival products [0000050863-26-000011:0171]. In October 2024 the Court of Justice dismissed the EC's appeal on rebates, which upheld the General Court's judgment [0000050863-26-000011:0171].
In September 2023 the EC imposed a €376 million ($401 million) fine based on the finding about payments to prevent sales of rival products [0000050863-26-000011:0172]. Intel appealed, and in December 2025 the General Court reduced the fine to €237 million ($277 million) [0000050863-26-000011:0172]. Intel may appeal that decision to the Court of Justice [0000050863-26-000011:0172].
As of December 27, 2025, Intel had accrued approximately $311 million for the fine, including foreign currency revaluation effects and accrued interest [0000050863-26-000011:0172][0000050863-26-000011:0171]. Intel says it cannot reasonably estimate any potential loss in excess of that amount, given the procedural posture and nature of the proceedings [0000050863-26-000011:0172]. In 2025 Intel recorded a $163 million benefit from reducing the previously accrued $401 million fine [0000050863-26-000011:0049]. The fine remains unpaid on appeal, its payment is guaranteed by a third party, and Intel funded that guarantee in 2025 by depositing $340 million in legally restricted accounts [0000050863-26-000011:0049][0000050863-26-000011:0136].

questions.question: What is the current status of the securities class action and related derivative lawsuits against NVIDIA over cryptocurrency-mining demand, per its FY2026 10-K?

answer.text:
The securities class action, In Re NVIDIA Corporation Securities Litigation (4:18-cv-07669-HSG), alleges that NVIDIA and certain executives made materially false or misleading statements about channel inventory and the impact of cryptocurrency mining on GPU demand between May 10, 2017 and November 14, 2018 [0001045810-26-000021:0115]. The district court dismissed the complaint on March 2, 2021, and plaintiffs appealed to the Ninth Circuit [0001045810-26-000021:0115]. On August 25, 2023, a majority of a Ninth Circuit panel affirmed in part and reversed in part the dismissal [0001045810-26-000021:0115]. The Supreme Court dismissed NVIDIA's writ of certiorari as improvidently granted on December 11, 2024, and issued judgment on January 13, 2025 [0001045810-26-000021:0116]. The Ninth Circuit's judgment took effect on February 20, 2025, and the case was remanded to the district court for further proceedings [0001045810-26-000021:0116]. The risk factors section says NVIDIA is still defending this securities class action [0001045810-26-000021:0052].
The derivative suit in the Northern District of California (4:19-cv-00341-HSG) was stayed pending the appeal in the securities action [0001045810-26-000021:0116]. The court administratively closed it on February 22, 2022, and said it would reopen the case once the appeal is resolved, but it has not yet been reopened [0001045810-26-000021:0116]. The plaintiffs seek unspecified damages and governance reforms [0001045810-26-000021:0116].
Huang, were also stayed [0001045810-26-000021:0116]. On March 7, 2025, the district court adopted the parties' stipulation to extend the stay until the final and complete resolution of the securities class action [0001045810-26-000021:0116]. The Delaware plaintiffs seek unspecified damages, disgorgement of profits from NVIDIA stock sales, and unspecified corporate governance measures [0001045810-26-000021:0116].

questions.question: What risks does NVIDIA's FY2026 10-K associate with its acquisitions and strategic investments, including its planned OpenAI deal?

answer.text:
NVIDIA says acquisitions and investments involve significant challenges and risks and could impair its ability to grow its business, develop new products or sell its products, and ultimately hurt its financial results [0001045810-26-000021:0034]. Pursuing one transaction may limit its ability to enter other transactions [0001045810-26-000021:0034]. Technology could also evolve and make an acquisition less attractive [0001045810-26-000021:0034]. Regulators could impose conditions that reduce an acquisition's ultimate value, and harm to its perceived ability to complete acquisitions could make future ones more difficult, complex or expensive [0001045810-26-000021:0034].
On investments, NVIDIA says they could create volatility and fluctuations in its results, with realized and unrealized gains or losses, and it could lose up to the full value of an investment [0001045810-26-000021:0034]. Many investee companies may not achieve profitability in the near term, or at all, and there is no guarantee of a return [0001045810-26-000021:0034]. questions.question: Why did NVIDIA's gross margin decrease in fiscal year 2026?

answer.text:
NVIDIA's gross margin decreased to 71.1% in fiscal year 2026 from 75.0% in fiscal year 2025 [0001045810-26-000021:0068]. The filing attributes the decline to the business model transitioning from offering Hopper HGX systems to Blackwell full-scale datacenter solutions [0001045810-26-000021:0068][0001045810-26-000021:0063]. It was also affected by a $4.5 billion charge associated with H20 excess inventory and purchase obligations in the first quarter of fiscal year 2026 [0001045810-26-000021:0068].
Provisions for inventory and excess inventory purchase obligations totaled $7.2 billion in fiscal year 2026, compared with $3.7 billion in fiscal year 2025, and included the $4.5 billion H20 charge [0001045810-26-000021:0068]. Sales of previously reserved inventory and settlements of excess inventory purchase obligations resulted in a provision release of $1.5 billion in fiscal year 2026 [0001045810-26-000021:0068]. The net effect of inventory provisions and sales of items previously written down was an unfavorable impact of 2.6% on gross margin in fiscal year 2026, versus 2.3% in fiscal year 2025 [0001045810-26-000021:0068].

questions.question: How do NVIDIA (fiscal 2026 10-K), AMD (fiscal 2025 10-K) and Intel (fiscal 2025 10-K) each describe their reliance on TSMC?

answer.text:
AMD says it relies on TSMC for the production of all wafers for its microprocessor and GPU products at 7 nm or smaller nodes [0000002488-26-000018:0029]. It says that if TSMC cannot make enough wafers at those nodes, or enough of its newest IC products, to meet customer demand, its business could be materially adversely affected [0000002488-26-000018:0029]. AMD is presently focusing its 7 nm and lower microprocessor and GPU portfolio on TSMC's processes [0000002488-26-000018:0032]. It describes TSMC as the foundry that manufactures its newest IC products [0000002488-26-000018:0032]. AMD also uses TSMC, UMC and Samsung for its programmable logic devices [0000002488-26-000018:0029].
Intel says its products are predominantly made in its own facilities, but it has also used third-party foundry capacity, including at TSMC, which it calls one of its key foundry competitors [0000050863-26-000011:0018]. It uses TSMC for various tiles or for an entire product where that is advantageous for cost, performance, schedule or other considerations [0000050863-26-000011:0018]. It expects to keep using TSMC and other third-party foundries for key tiles in a number of current and future products [0000050863-26-000011:0018].
Intel adds that some of its newer and higher-end products use tiles made by TSMC [0000050863-26-000011:0063]. If TSMC's supply were interrupted, Intel would be unable to complete assembly of products needing those tiles until it could design and source replacements, which would likely mean a substantial delay [0000050863-26-000011:0063].
Intel also says that if it cannot secure a significant external foundry customer for Intel 14A, it may pause or discontinue that node and successor leading-edge nodes [0000050863-26-000011:0008]. In that case it expects over time to shift manufacturing to third-party foundries, particularly TSMC, for nodes beyond Intel 18A and Intel 18A-P [0000050863-26-000011:0008][0000050863-26-000011:0065]. Intel states that it has no long-term contract with TSMC [0000050863-26-000011:0065].

questions.question: In calendar 2024, how did data center revenue growth compare between AMD (fiscal 2024) and NVIDIA (fiscal 2025), and what drove it at each company?

answer.text:
AMD's Data Center net revenue was $12.6 billion in fiscal 2024, up 94% from $6.5 billion in 2023 [0000002488-25-000012:0068]. AMD attributed the increase to higher sales of AMD Instinct GPUs and AMD EPYC CPUs [0000002488-25-000012:0073]. AMD also said demand for its Data Center AI accelerators was very strong, led by large hyperscale cloud customers deploying AMD Instinct MI300X GPU accelerators [0000002488-25-000012:0068].
It says Data Center revenue was up 154% from a year ago and up 16% sequentially [0001045810-24-000264:0034]. NVIDIA said this growth was driven by demand for its Hopper GPU computing platform for training and inferencing of large language models, recommendation engines and generative AI applications [0001045810-24-000264:0034]. It added that year-on-year growth came from all customer types and from both compute and networking revenue [0001045810-24-000264:0034]. Data Center compute revenue was $22.6 billion, up 162% from a year ago, and networking revenue was $3.7 billion, up 114% [0001045810-24-000264:0034].

questions.question: What agreements with OpenAI do AMD's fiscal 2025 10-K and NVIDIA's fiscal 2026 10-K disclose, and how far had each progressed?

answer.text:
AMD's fiscal 2025 10-K discloses a product purchase agreement with OpenAI OpCo, LLC, entered into in October 2025, to deploy 6 gigawatts of AMD GPUs, with the first gigawatt of capacity powered by AMD Instinct MI450 series products [0000002488-26-000018:0072][0000002488-26-000018:0005]. questions.question: AMD's fiscal 2025 10-K names Altera as a competitor. What happened to Intel's ownership of Altera in 2025, and how does Intel now account for it?

answer.text:
AMD's fiscal 2025 10-K names Altera as a competitor in its Data Center segment, with FPGA and adaptive SoC server products, and in its Embedded segment as a primary FPGA competitor [0000002488-26-000018:0014].
On April 14, 2025, Intel signed a transaction agreement with SLP VII Gryphon Aggregator, L.P., an affiliate of SLP, to sell 51% of Altera's issued and outstanding common stock, and Altera was then a wholly owned subsidiary [0000050863-26-000011:0145]. Intel completed the divestiture of that 51% on September 12, 2025, for net purchase consideration of $4.3 billion [0000050863-26-000011:0145]. Intel retained a 49% minority investment [0000050863-26-000011:0146]. As of December 27, 2025, Intel's ownership interest was 48% [0000050863-26-000011:0145].
Intel concluded that Altera is a VIE for which it is not the primary beneficiary, because the governance structure does not let Intel direct the activities that most significantly affect Altera's economic performance [0000050863-26-000011:0146]. Intel therefore deconsolidated Altera from its Consolidated Financial Statements at the September 12, 2025 close date [0000050863-26-000011:0146]. Altera's results were included in Intel's "all other" category through September 11, 2025 [0000050863-26-000011:0039].
The retained interest is accounted for under the equity method and classified within equity investments in the Consolidated Balance Sheets [0000050863-26-000011:0145]. Intel set its fair value by reference to Altera's equity value under the transaction agreement, at $3.2 billion, and recognized it as a non-cash investing activity in 2025 [0000050863-26-000011:0146]. The carrying value was $3.2 billion as of December 27, 2025 [0000050863-26-000011:0145].
The sale produced a pre-tax gain of $5.6 billion, recognized within interest and other, net, in 2025 [0000050863-26-000011:0146]. Approximately $2.1 billion of that gain came from remeasuring the retained investment to fair value at the close date [0000050863-26-000011:0147].

questions.question: How did the growth rates and stated drivers of NVIDIA's Gaming and Professional Visualization revenue in fiscal year 2026 compare with fiscal year 2025?

answer.text:
Gaming revenue rose 41% in fiscal year 2026, driven by strong Blackwell demand [0001045810-26-000021:0063]. In fiscal year 2025, Gaming revenue rose 9%, driven by sales of GeForce RTX 40 Series GPUs [0001045810-25-000023:0064]. Gaming growth was therefore much faster in fiscal year 2026, and the driver moved from the RTX 40 Series to Blackwell [0001045810-26-000021:0063][0001045810-25-000023:0064]. For fiscal year 2026 the filing also says supply constraints are expected to be a headwind to Gaming in the first quarter of fiscal 2027 and beyond [0001045810-26-000021:0063].
Professional Visualization revenue rose 70% in fiscal year 2026, driven by exceptional demand for Blackwell and the launch of the new DGX Spark [0001045810-26-000021:0063]. In fiscal year 2025 it rose 21%, driven by the continued ramp of Ada RTX GPU workstations for uses such as generative AI-powered design, simulation and engineering [0001045810-25-000023:0064]. Growth was therefore much higher in fiscal year 2026, and the drivers moved from Ada RTX workstations to Blackwell and DGX Spark [0001045810-26-000021:0063][0001045810-25-000023:0064].

questions.question: What did AMD say drove its Data Center segment revenue growth in the second quarter of 2024, and how did the drivers and segment profitability differ in the second quarter of 2025?

answer.text:
In the second quarter of 2024, AMD's Data Center net revenue was $2.8 billion, up 115% from $1.3 billion a year earlier, driven primarily by the steep ramp of AMD Instinct GPU shipments and strong growth in 4th Gen AMD EPYC CPU sales [0000002488-24-000123:0026]. Data Center operating income for that quarter was $743 million, compared with $147 million in the prior year period, with the increase primarily driven by higher revenue [0000002488-24-000123:0026].
In the second quarter of 2025, Data Center net revenue was $3.2 billion, up 14% from $2.8 billion in the prior year period, and AMD attributed the increase primarily to growth in AMD EPYC CPU sales [0000002488-25-000108:0033]. Unlike in 2024, the 2025 filing does not cite Instinct GPU shipments as a driver of the increase [0000002488-25-000108:0033].
Data Center operating loss was $155 million for the three months ended June 28, 2025, compared with operating income of $743 million a year earlier [0000002488-25-000108:0033]. AMD said the decrease was primarily due to approximately $800 million of inventory and related charges tied to the U.S. government export control on AMD Instinct MI308 GPU products, along with higher R&D expense [0000002488-25-000108:0033].

questions.question: How did the server volume and server ASP trends behind Intel's DCAI revenue in the second quarter of 2025 compare with those in the second quarter of 2024, and what did Intel give as the reasons?

answer.text:
In Q2 2025, DCAI revenue increased $134 million from Q2 2024, primarily driven by higher server revenue due to higher hyperscale customer-related demand, which contributed to a 13% increase in server volume [0000050863-25-000109:0044]. Server ASPs decreased 8% from Q2 2024, primarily due to pricing actions taken in a competitive environment [0000050863-25-000109:0044].
In Q2 2024, by contrast, DCAI revenue was $3.0 billion, down $110 million from Q2 2023, driven by a decrease in server revenue [0000050863-24-000124:0040]. Server volume decreased 22% in Q2 2024 due to lower demand in a competitive environment and a higher mix of high core count products [0000050863-24-000124:0040]. Server ASPs increased 23% in Q2 2024, primarily due to a lower mix of hyperscale customer-related revenue and a higher mix of high core count products [0000050863-24-000124:0040].
So the pattern reversed: the Q2 2025 filing reports server volume up 13% and ASPs down 8% against Q2 2024, while the Q2 2024 filing reported volume down 22% and ASPs up 23% against Q2 2023 [0000050863-25-000109:0044][0000050863-24-000124:0040].

questions.question: Intel's fiscal 2024 10-K disclosed capital expenditure commitments for 2025. How did Intel's actual 2025 additions to property, plant and equipment, reported in the fiscal 2025 10-K, compare with that commitment and with 2024 spending, and how did Intel explain the change in investing cash flows?

answer.text:
The fiscal 2024 10-K said that, as of December 28, 2024, Intel had commitments for capital expenditures of $14.0 billion for 2025, with a further $6.0 billion committed in the long term [0000050863-25-000009:0042]. In the fiscal 2025 10-K cash flow statement, investing-activity additions to property, plant and equipment were $14,646 million in 2025, which is slightly above the $14.0 billion committed for 2025 [0000050863-26-000011:0103][0000050863-25-000009:0042]. That 2025 figure is well below the $23,944 million of investing-activity additions in 2024 [0000050863-26-000011:0103]. Financing activities also included additions to property, plant and equipment of $3,026 million in 2025, up from $1,178 million in 2024 [0000050863-26-000011:0103].
Net cash used for investing activities was $14,821 million in 2025 compared with $18,256 million in 2024 [0000050863-26-000011:0050]. Intel attributed the decrease mainly to lower capital expenditures, higher proceeds from the divestitures of its Altera and NAND memory businesses, and other cash-favorable investing activity [0000050863-26-000011:0050]. It said these favorable effects were partly offset by higher purchases of short-term investments (net of sales and maturities), lower sales of equity investments, and lower proceeds from capital-related government incentives [0000050863-26-000011:0050].
