questions.question: How did Intel Foundry's third-quarter operating loss move from Q3 2023 to Q3 2024 to Q3 2025, and what were the main drivers of each change?

answer.text:
Intel Foundry's operating loss was $1.4 billion in Q3 2023 ($1,407 million) and $5.8 billion in Q3 2024 ($5,844 million as reported in the FY2024 Q3 10-Q) [0000050863-24-000149:0047]. It narrowed to $2,321 million in Q3 2025 [0000050863-25-000179:0055]. The FY2025 Q3 10-Q shows the Q3 2024 comparative as $5,799 million [0000050863-25-000179:0055].
The largest driver was $3,095 million of higher period charges for non-cash impairments and accelerated depreciation on certain manufacturing assets, a substantial majority of which related to the Intel 7 process node [0000050863-24-000149:0047]. - $976 million lower intersegment product and services profit, mainly from lower intersegment ASPs, lower intersegment samples and lower external revenue [0000050863-24-000149:0047].
- $297 million higher operating expenses, driven by increased investment in process technology [0000050863-24-000149:0047].
- $136 million higher period charges, primarily factory start-up costs [0000050863-24-000149:0047].
- A $67 million favorable "other" item [0000050863-24-000149:0047].
Revenue was $4,235 million in Q3 2025 versus $4,339 million in Q3 2024, while cost of sales and operating expenses fell from $10,138 million to $6,556 million [0000050863-25-000179:0055]. The operating loss margin improved from (134)% to (55)% [0000050863-25-000179:0055].
External revenue fell $23 million to $32 million [0000050863-25-000179:0055].
answer.raw_text:
STATUS: answered

Intel Foundry's operating loss was $1.4 billion in Q3 2023 ($1,407 million) and $5.8 billion in Q3 2024 ($5,844 million as reported in the FY2024 Q3 10-Q) [0000050863-24-000149:0047]. It narrowed to $2,321 million in Q3 2025 [0000050863-25-000179:0055]. The FY2025 Q3 10-Q shows the Q3 2024 comparative as $5,799 million [0000050863-25-000179:0055].

From Q3 2023 to Q3 2024, the loss grew by about $4.4 billion. The largest driver was $3,095 million of higher period charges for non-cash impairments and accelerated depreciation on certain manufacturing assets, a substantial majority of which related to the Intel 7 process node [0000050863-24-000149:0047]. Other drivers were:
- $976 million lower intersegment product and services profit, mainly from lower intersegment ASPs, lower intersegment samples and lower external revenue [0000050863-24-000149:0047].
- $297 million higher operating expenses, driven by increased investment in process technology [0000050863-24-000149:0047].
- $136 million higher period charges, primarily factory start-up costs [0000050863-24-000149:0047].
- A $67 million favorable "other" item [0000050863-24-000149:0047].

From Q3 2024 to Q3 2025, the loss narrowed. Revenue was $4,235 million in Q3 2025 versus $4,339 million in Q3 2024, while cost of sales and operating expenses fell from $10,138 million to $6,556 million [0000050863-25-000179:0055]. The operating loss margin improved from (134)% to (55)% [0000050863-25-000179:0055].

On the revenue side, Q3 2025 revenue was down $104 million. Intersegment revenue fell $81 million, primarily on lower front-end services revenue and lower sample revenue, partly offset by higher intersegment back-end services revenue. External revenue fell $23 million to $32 million [0000050863-25-000179:0055].

questions.question: How did Intel's plans for its Ohio and Germany fabs, as described in its fiscal 2024 10-K, change by the time of its fiscal 2025 10-K?

answer.text:
It had slowed the completion of the Ohio facility and put the Germany plans on hold, because it had reassessed demand and its "shell ahead" status and sought to limit capital expenditures given recent financial results [0000050863-25-000009:0014].
In the fiscal 2025 10-K, Intel said that in 2025 it had slowed the pace of construction for its new Ohio wafer fabrication facility and discontinued planned expansions in Germany (fab) and Poland (assembly and test facility) [0000050863-26-000011:0008]. The fiscal 2025 filing also says Intel recognized $123 million of capital grants in 2025 related to two new leading-edge chip factories in Ohio [0000050863-26-000011:0132].

In the fiscal 2025 10-K, Intel said that in 2025 it had slowed the pace of construction for its new Ohio wafer fabrication facility and discontinued planned expansions in Germany (fab) and Poland (assembly and test facility) [0000050863-26-000011:0008]. questions.question: Intel's client (notebook and desktop) revenue fell in the first quarter of 2025. How does the Q1 2025 10-Q explain the decline, and what did the Q1 2024 10-Q report about client volumes, revenue and ASPs in that prior-year quarter?

answer.text:
The Q1 2025 10-Q says CCG revenue decreased 8% from Q1 2024, primarily due to lower client revenue driven by lower Q1 2025 client volumes [0000050863-25-000074:0041]. It attributes those lower volumes primarily to the absence of incremental purchasing incentives offered to certain customers in Q1 2024 [0000050863-25-000074:0041]. Those incentives, particularly in CCG, contributed approximately $1.6 billion to revenue during Q1 2024 and were insignificant in Q1 2025 [0000050863-25-000074:0041].
The Q1 2024 10-Q reported that notebook revenue was $4.7 billion, up $1.3 billion from Q1 2023, and desktop revenue was $2.5 billion, up $582 million from Q1 2023 [0000050863-24-000076:0034]. Notebook volume increased 39% and desktop volume increased 29% in Q1 2024 as customer inventory levels normalized compared to higher levels in Q1 2023 [0000050863-24-000076:0034]. Notebook and desktop ASPs were roughly flat with Q1 2023 [0000050863-24-000076:0034]. The segment table shows Q1 2024 desktop revenue of $2,461 million and notebook revenue of $4,681 million, within total CCG revenue of $7,533 million [0000050863-24-000076:0014]. That filing also said CCG revenue increased 31% from Q1 2023, and that incentives contributed approximately $1.6 billion to revenue in Q1 2024 compared with approximately $900 million in Q1 2023 [0000050863-24-000076:0039].
